BEIJING: China's factory activity unexpectedly dropped in October, its third contraction in four months, a government survey showed on Saturday (Oct 31), hurt by soft demand for exports as well as goods at home. The official manufacturing purchasing managers' index (PMI) fell to 49.3 from 50.1 in September, according to data from the National Bureau of Statistics. That missed a forecast for 50.0 from a Reuters poll. Factory activity weakened as overseas Christmas-related orders, which were front-loaded in September, cooled in October. It was also hurt when consumer spending, which climbed during China's long National Day holiday in the first week of October, fizzled out after, in a return to its long-stagnant state. "Insufficient demand is increasing downward pressure on the economy," said Zhang Liqun, an analyst with the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing, adding that policymakers should take the problem seriously and step up measures as soon as possible.

Sub-indexes for new orders overall and for new export orders both stayed in contraction territory in October. Production and purchasing activity also slipped into contraction from expansion. The non-manufacturing PMI, which covers services and construction, also dropped to 49.7 from 50.2 in September. The readings are compiled based on purchasing managers' reports about whether conditions improved, worsened or were unchanged in areas such as new orders, output and employment compared with the previous month. A reading above 50 signals expansion, while one below 50 indicates contraction. Some sectors within manufacturing were doing well. Production and new orders sub-indexes for railway, shipbuilding, aerospace equipment, and computer, communications and electronics manufacturing were all at or above 53.0, the survey showed. AI-related firms in particular have reported strong earnings growth. Zhongji Innolight, a maker of high-speed optical modules that connect servers and switches in AI data centres, posted a near tripling in third-quarter net profit. But the lacklustre domestic market and rising costs have weighed on many old-school manufacturers and property-linked firms. Custom furniture maker Oppein Home, for example, saw net profit plunge 80 per cent during the quarter. China's economy is, however, expected to meet the country's 4.5-5.0 per cent annual growth target without additional stimulus measures after third-quarter growth rebounded to 4.5 per cent from 4.3 per cent in April-June.

Source: Reuters/kl

FAST

SANTA SUSANNA, Spain, Oct 30 : Nonagenarian Japanese bodybuilder Toshisuke Kanazawa took to the stage on Spain's Costa del Maresme on Friday, aiming to prove that age is no barrier to peak physical fitness. The 90-year-old travelled to the coastal town of Santa Susanna to compete against rivals decades his junior in the masters category for athletes aged 50 and older in a competition held by the International Fitness and Bodybuilding Federation. Backstage, Kanazawa mirrored the preparations of younger competitors, warming up with his team and applying spray tan before flexing under the stage lights. "I like to try doing things that nobody else has done, and more than anything I want to pursue bodybuilding for the rest of my life," Kanazawa said.

Kanazawa credits his longevity and conditioning to strict dietary habits, saying that a routine established decades ago has kept him robust. "This is something I've been researching and want to learn more about. But ever since I turned 50, I've been building muscle by eating a purely Japanese diet: brown rice, natto (a fermented soya bean dish)), and miso soup," he said. "It's really the classic Japanese way of eating. And thanks to that, I've gone 90 years without ever getting sick." Though he did not finish on the podium, Kanazawa remains focused on pushing the sport's boundaries, outlining plans for one final appearance before stepping away from competition. "I'm thinking I might give it one more go at 93. After that, I'll probably have to retire," he said. "As you get older, you start developing wrinkles, quite a lot of them. In Japan, there's this idea that once you get those wrinkles, it just doesn't look very good anymore." Ultimately, Kanazawa hopes his perseverance inspires older generations to remain active and challenge conventional limits. "Once you set your mind to something, you need to develop the mental strength and determination to see it through no matter what," Kanazawa said. "I want people to work hard just as I have. I believe that if they do, we'll see more people like me even as they get older. That's what I hope for, and I want to be a good role model."

Source: Reuters

WASHINGTON, Oct 30 : A US federal appeals court on Friday reinstated a jury's verdict against the National Football League in an antitrust lawsuit claiming it overcharged subscribers to its Sunday Ticket game telecasts for more than a decade, but said the league can have a new trial on damages. The ruling by the San Francisco-based 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals overturned a lower court judge in California who had thrown out a $4.7 billion verdict against the NFL after the trial in 2024. The NFL in a statement said it is disappointed by the decision and is weighing its options for further court review of the decision. It defended the televised broadcast strategy as the "most fan-friendly distribution model" in sports and entertainment.  Lawyers for the plaintiffs — residential subscribers and commercial businesses — did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

"Sunday Ticket" is the only broadcast option for NFL fans who want to watch their teams play out-of-market games. The subscribers alleged "Sunday Ticket" prices were inflated to limit subscriptions and protect fees for distribution rights that broadcast networks paid to air games in local markets. A Los Angeles federal jury awarded $4.6 billion in damages to residential subscribers and $96.9 million for commercial subscribers like bars and restaurants. But US District Judge Philip Gutierrez overturned the verdict in 2024, throwing out testimony by two key witnesses and finding that evidence did not support the damages. The NFL had called the damages amount "nonsensical" and argued that the subscribers never proved with reliable evidence that the league’s Sunday Ticket arrangements actually caused them any harm. In its ruling on Friday, the appeals court concluded the trial judge was wrong to reject the plaintiffs' expert witnesses. A jury verdict "must stand unless it is clearly not supported by the evidence," the appeals court said. But the panel said the jury's damages award was based "on its improper consideration of the evidence rather than according to the district court’s instructions."

Source: Reuters

Oct 30 : Fallon Sherrock beat Luke Littler to claim a £501,000 ($671,089) prize in a live Netflix darts special on Friday, producing a dramatic upset in front of a global audience at Manchester Central. Sherrock finished from 43 on double top to win a single leg of 501 against Littler, ending the event after 14 previous challengers had failed to beat the two-time world champion. The 32-year-old from Milton Keynes won the bull-off to earn the throw and produced a 15-dart leg under intense pressure, with the format designed to conclude as soon as a challenger defeated Littler. Her winning dart sparked celebrations inside the arena as Sherrock, one of the most recognisable players in women's darts, secured the biggest prize of her career.

"It's the first time he's been to anything. It was lovely. Sorry, I'm just so lost for words right now. It was a great moment and I'll memorise this forever." Sherrock, a qualified hairdresser, has become a trailblazing figure in the sport since making history at the 2020 PDC World Darts Championship in December 2019. Known as the "Queen of the Palace", she became the first woman to win a match at the tournament when she beat Ted Evetts, before following it with another victory over Mensur Suljovic. "World class," Littler said. "I've enjoyed every bit of it — the ad, the photo shoots, just everything leading up to this. It's been good. Maybe Netflix, we can do it again next year." Oct 30 : Crypto exchanges are taking quick action to bolster their defenses and urging greater industry-wide information-sharing after a record $6.3 billion hack of Binance exposed their vulnerability just as they become more embedded in mainstream finance. Coinbase said it made adjustments to its systems that store cryptocurrency keys offline "solely out of an abundance of caution," while Kraken said it was monitoring industry incidents for lessons it could apply to its defenses. But the industry will need to move urgently, analysts and industry executives said, as President Donald Trump's regulators promote deeper integration of digital assets into the financial system, raising the stakes for an industry with a history of big hacks. "For crypto to reach its full potential, the security situation must be addressed immediately," said Chris Perkins, Franklin Templeton's head of crypto.

Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, halted withdrawals after Thursday's attack — which analysts blamed on North Korea — and said it would use company funds to cover the losses. Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said on X that the “complex attack” may have begun with a compromised software engineer’s laptop, giving hackers access to systems used to process withdrawals. The company later found additional breaches, while software designed to erase traces of the attack hampered the investigation. Rival crypto exchanges moved quickly on Friday to shore up their own systems and to reassure customers that their tokens were safe “Full-time teams at Kraken look for potential vulnerabilities every day,” a Kraken spokesperson said. Still, even as the industry reeled from the biggest cryptocurrency heist of all time, executives expressed confidence that Binance had sufficient resources to cover the losses and that the hack would not have broader financial repercussions. Bitcoin fell more than 4 per cent on Thursday while ether, the second-largest cryptocurrency, fell more than 5 per cent, although both tokens recovered some of that ground on Friday. "Our expectation is the industry writ large will actually not suffer material losses, even though Binance is obviously going to have to deal with the exploit directly," said Josh Riezman, chief legal and strategy officer at crypto firm GSR. The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis. North Korea routinely denies involvement in cryptocurrency thefts, and its mission in Geneva did not respond to requests for comment. HACK INVOLVES SOCIAL ENGINEERING, MONEY LAUNDERING While much remains unclear, social engineering, a common tactic in which hackers trick victims into revealing sensitive information or granting access to systems, may have been involved in compromising the laptop, security experts said. Harry Donnelly, CEO of Circuit, a crypto risk infrastructure company, said companies are planning more employee training to guard against social engineering attacks. In such attacks, hackers race to launder the funds before the exchange detects the breach and token issuers freeze assets. Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion linked to Binance, while Circle said it froze $800 million. Bitcoin and ether cannot be frozen because no single entity controls the coins. Chainalysis said the hackers appeared to be using sophisticated laundering patterns it had not seen before. On Friday, some crypto exchange executives called for the industry to develop a coordinated hack detection system. "We need a real-time alert system that allows participants to share information immediately when a hack occurs, coordinate a rapid response, and temporarily freeze suspected stolen funds," said Star Xu, CEO of crypto exchange OKX, in a post on X. GSR's Riezman added that the Binance hack could spur the industry to act: "As we're at this kind of confluence moment for traditional finance and digital assets, I think it's obviously important that we continue to improve, and I think this, if anything, will be a catalyst for that."

Source: Reuters

Oct 30 : OpenAI has slashed the target for its latest funding round by $10 billion amid a selloff in tech stocks driven by AI worries, the Financial Times reported on Friday, citing people with knowledge of the matter. The ChatGPT maker is now seeking about $20 billion and its desired valuation has dropped to $1.25 trillion from $1.4 billion, the report said. OpenAI set a Friday deadline for investors to commit to the funding round, but the "first close" is expected to raise less than $20 billion after some investors reduced their allocations, it added. A consortium of UAE investors that includes state-backed technology fund MGX is expected to be the largest participant in the round, and as part of the deal, OpenAI would gain the option to lease newly developed computing capacity in the region, the newspaper added.

Venture capital firms including Founders Fund, Coatue, Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz are also expected to participate, according to the report. Wealthy individuals will have the option to invest in a subsequent retail offering at a $1.25 trillion valuation, the FT added. OpenAI, MGX, Coatue, Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment outside regular business hours. Founders Fund could not be reached for comment. US tech stocks have suffered a rout amid growing worries over massive spending on AI. The tech-heavy Nasdaq index dropped 2.9 per cent on Friday and is down 7.8 per cent from its all-time closing high reached on October 6. OpenAI, which is pursuing a listing in 2027, has been keen to close the funding round partly to get ahead of Anthropic's imminent listing as the two are tapping a similar investor base, Reuters has reported.

MEXICO CITY, Oct 30 : Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu vehemently dismissed reports that excessive salary demands from Oliver Bearman's camp were holding up the British driver's contract extension, accusing those spreading the claims of inventing stories to generate clicks. Bearman's future with US-owned Haas has been in the spotlight after the Formula One team confirmed Brazilian Rafael Camara would replace Esteban Ocon for 2027 but stopped short of announcing a new deal for the 21-year-old, whose contract is due to expire at the end of the season. Some reports have suggested Bearman is seeking an annual salary of six million euros but Komatsu reacted angrily when the figure was put to him. "I have no idea where that comes from. Honestly. I've experienced this sometimes this season as well. Some people say there's no smoke without fire, but really, some people invent the story," Komatsu told reporters on Friday ahead of Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix.

Okay, I want to get some more clicks, so they cut and paste those stories and keep running with it." Both parties want to extend but have declined to say what is holding up an announcement. "I don't think I can go into the details of what's the hold-up, but it's very clear from both parties, from Ollie's side and our side they want to continue working together," he said. "We're trying to find a solution to work together next year, and I'm sure we will." Bearman returns to Mexico with fond memories after finishing fourth at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez last year, matching Haas's best-ever result in Formula One. Komatsu spoke highly of the Ferrari-backed Briton's progress since his rookie season. "I just see a huge maturity and growth in his leadership capability, and he's only 21 years old. LE HAVRE, France, Oct 30 : Flying fullback Achraf Hakimi grabbed a hat-trick as Paris St Germain went on the rampage to thrash bottom-placed Le Havre 5-1 and extend their Ligue 1 lead on Friday. The European champions, who have several regulars out injured, could afford to leave more of their key players on the bench and still come away with an impressive victory as they moved to 20 points from their opening nine league fixtures. They are two ahead of Lille and four above third-placed Rennes, who have 16 points. Lille moved above Rennes into second after a late goal from veteran Olivier Giroud, who came off the bench to score an 86th minute winner at home for a 1-0 derby victory over RC Lens.  Rennes were handed a 5-2 drubbing at Nice, who continued their improving form with a fourth win in five outings.

Elye Wahi netted a hat-trick for Nice, who moved up to seventh after last season narrowly avoiding relegation. On top of his three goals at Stade Oceane, Hakimi had two assists for the goals scored by Mika Godts and Senny Mayulu after Josh Maja had given the hosts the lead. It was PSG's ninth consecutive victory in all competitions. Le Havre suffered a fifth consecutive defeat and sit bottom with two points but they briefly dared to believe as Maja handed them an early lead. Hakimi set up Godts for the equaliser before putting his side ahead in the 28th minute with a shot in at the near post. The Morocco international then netted from a free kick into the bottom corner in the 55th minute before being at the centre of a counter attack that saw Mayulu make it 4-1 in the 62nd minute.  Hakimi completed his hat-trick with a deflected effort in the 69th minute. "I am happy because some players had very little playing time. If we want to win trophies, we need everyone,” said PSG coach Luis Enrique.  "With injuries, opportunities arise. That was particularly the case tonight for Quentin Ndjantou and David Boly, who made his Ligue 1 debut. Wahi’s hat-trick for Nice was made up of two first half penalties and a 73rd minute first time finish.

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town)

Source: Reuters
